paper_title: Token-Level Uncertainty Estimation for Large Language Model Reasoning
caption: Left: Uncertainty estimations in different token decoding temperature . Right: Influence of token decoding temperature on uncertainty-based AUROC scores.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between decoding temperature and uncertainty estimations for three different models, labeled AU, TU, and EU. The x-axis is labeled “Decoding Temperature” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.8 with tick labels every 0.2 units. The y-axis is not explicitly labeled, but has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.175 with tick labels every 0.025 units. The AU model is represented by a red line with circular markers; beginning at a value of approximately 0.126 at a decoding temperature of 0.0, it declines to 0.113 at a temperature of 0.2, rises to 0.125 at 0.4, and increases to approximately 0.143 at a decoding temperature of 0.8. The TU model is shown as a blue line with circular markers, starting at a value of approximately 0.127 at a decoding temperature of 0.0, declining to 0.121 at a temperature of 0.2, rising to 0.128 at 0.4, and increasing to approximately 0.137 at a decoding temperature of 0.8. The EU model is represented by a green line with circular markers, which remains relatively constant around a value of approximately 0.002 across the entire range of decoding temperatures from 0.0 to 0.8.
